results.reason: The deliverable incorrectly states the lock-up expires on 13 April 2027 (365 days after 13 April 2026 Prospectus date), not 1 May 2027 (365 days after 1 May 2026). The Prospectus is dated 1 May 2026 per prospectus_extract.md clause 1.1, not 13 April 2026.

The deliverable completely misses this critical issue. The comfort letter cut-off date is 22 April 2026 (per comfort_letter.md clause 1.1 and 6.1), but the Underwriting Agreement Clause 7(b) requires the comfort letter to be dated no earlier than 3 business days before the Pricing Date (1 May 2026), meaning 28 April 2026. The 22 April 2026 cut-off is 6 days too early, requiring a bring-down letter. The deliverable incorrectly calculates 28 April 2026 as the deadline without recognizing the conflict with the 22 April 2026 cut-off.

The deliverable fails to identify the $6,250,000 interest-free loan to director Marcus Thackeray disclosed in board_minutes.md clause 7. This material related party transaction is not mentioned anywhere in the deliverable, despite being required for Prospectus disclosure and constituting a significant time-sensitive obligation (repayable by 30 June 2031, requiring shareholder approval at next AGM).

The deliverable gives the lock-up as 365 days after 13 April 2026 (13 April 2027), not 365 days after 1 May 2026 (1 May 2027). The days remaining calculation of 365 days from 13 April 2026 is also incorrect—it should be 383 days to 1 May 2027, not 365 days to 13 April 2027.

The deliverable fails to identify that 1 May 2027 is a Saturday and does not calculate the next Business Day as 3 May 2027. The deliverable incorrectly states 13 April 2027 is a Tuesday without checking whether this is the correct lock-up expiration date or whether the actual expiration date (1 May 2027) falls on a weekend.
The deliverable opens with a 'Bottom Line' section containing overall conclusion and prioritized most critical risks before the detailed analysis, satisfying this formatting requirement.
